titre: Un Chien andalou (An Andalusian Dog) was meant to scandalize the public; the public loved it
accroche: Buñuel had filled his pockets with stones to defend himself against an audience he expected to be hostile. The audience loved the film.
contenu_vulgarise:
On June 6, 1929, at the Studio des Ursulines in Paris, Luis Buñuel presents *Un Chien andalou* (*An Andalusian Dog*), seventeen minutes shot in two weeks on a budget provided by his mother and edited by Buñuel himself, for lack of money to pay an editor. The film opens with a scene that has remained famous: a cloud slices across the moon, then a razor slices a young woman's eye. Buñuel himself would say he felt nauseated watching it again.

## Stones in his pockets

Buñuel writes the screenplay with Salvador Dalí with the explicit intention of shocking the intellectual bourgeoisie he loathed. Convinced that the audience would rise up against him on opening night, he arrives at the Studio des Ursulines with his pockets full of stones, ready, he would say later, to throw them at the audience in case of a scene. In the room that night: Pablo Picasso, Le Corbusier, Jean Cocteau, and the entire Surrealist group of André Breton.

Not a single stone is used. The audience acclaims the film. Buñuel, relieved that no violence has broken out, is nonetheless troubled by this unexpected triumph. Dalí, by contrast, says he is disappointed that the evening wasn't more eventful. In the preface he writes the same year for the published screenplay, Buñuel lets his bitterness burst out against the audience that received him so well.

Thanks to this triumph, Buñuel and Dalí are immediately welcomed into the very closed circle of the Surrealists by Breton himself. Bought by the owner of the Studio 28, the film stays on the bill for eight months. It is then, and not on opening night, that the real scandal begins: forty to fifty complaints are filed with the police demanding a ban. The film will never be banned, however. Legend intervenes afterward as well, even crediting the film with causing dizzy spells and fainting in the middle of screenings, an account that no source from the time supports.

## What this shifts

The scandal we now associate with *Un Chien andalou* therefore did not take place where it is usually placed, on opening night. It was built later, once the film was already established at the Studio 28, driven by police complaints and ever more spectacular rumors. What Buñuel had prepared as a frontal provocation, stones in his pockets, became an instant society success; it is its reputation, shaped after the fact by people who had not seen it, that ended up producing the scandal the film itself had not caused.

citation.texte: What can I do against those who go wild for any novelty, even when it goes against their deepest convictions, against a dishonest or complacent press, against this idiotic crowd that found beautiful or poetic what was, at bottom, only a desperate and passionate call to murder?

carte.punch: Buñuel had filled his pockets with stones, certain he would be attacked. The audience loved it.
carte.idee: For the premiere of Un Chien andalou in 1929, Buñuel fills his pockets with stones, certain that the bourgeois audience he was targeting would run wild. Picasso, Cocteau and the Surrealists instead acclaim the film. The real scandal doesn't break until eight months later.

quiz.question: According to the documented facts of 1929, what actually triggered the lasting scandal associated with Un Chien andalou?
choix: Police intervention on opening night, which interrupts the screening
Salvador Dalí's refusal to let his name be attached to the film's credits
The publication of a particularly vicious review in the Paris press, the day after the premiere
Dozens of complaints filed with the police during the eight-month run at the Studio 28, well after a triumphant premiere
quiz.explication: The premiere, at the Studio des Ursulines on June 6, 1929, was a triumph: the audience, including Picasso and the Surrealist group, acclaimed a film that Buñuel had thought so provocative that he had shown up with his pockets full of stones. The real scandal, with forty to fifty complaints filed with the police, came only later, during the film's run at the Studio 28.

quiz_supplementaire.question: How had Buñuel prepared, on opening night, for a hostile reaction from the audience that never came?
choix: He had hired bodyguards to protect the screening room
He had shown up with his pockets full of stones, ready to throw them at the audience
He had had the screening canceled as a precaution a few hours before the show
He had asked the police to discreetly watch the entrance of the theater
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Convinced that the audience would rise up against him, Buñuel arrived at the Studio des Ursulines with his pockets full of stones, ready to throw them at the audience in case of a scene.

quiz_supplementaire.question: How did Dalí react to the triumphant reception given to the film on opening night?
choix: He said he was disappointed that the evening wasn't more eventful
He left the room before the end, furious at the film's success
He demanded that his name be removed from the credits the next day
He publicly rejoiced at finally having won over the Paris bourgeoisie
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Unlike Buñuel, who was merely relieved that no violence had broken out, Dalí said he was disappointed that the evening wasn't more eventful than this unexpected triumph.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What happened to Un Chien andalou after it was bought by the owner of the Studio 28?
choix: The film was pulled from the bill after only two stormy screenings
The film was banned by the police after a week of screenings
The film stayed on the bill for eight months, while complaints piled up at the police
The film was re-edited by another director to soften its content
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Bought by the owner of the Studio 28, the film stays on the bill for eight months, a period during which forty to fifty complaints are filed with the police without its ever being banned.
